title: Michael Dell says AI needs safeguards and controls, and government has a role to play
source_used: The Times of India (relaying a CNBC interview)
key_facts: Michael Dell, chief executive of Dell Technologies, said on CNBC that AI needs strict 'safeguards and controls'.
He compared technology to fire: 'fire can heat your home. It can also burn down your whole village'.

He said both public and private sectors bear responsibility, called on AI developers to set 'bounded permissions' in their tools and acknowledged that government has a role, but declined to name specific laws, saying he is not a policymaker.
He does not believe AI will destroy humanity by 2030 and said 'It will be fine'.
He dismissed fears of an AI bubble: 'I don't think there's enough supply for it to be a bubble', pointing to a shortage of computing capacity and rising rental prices for Nvidia H100 chips.
The Times of India adds background on the AI-safety debate and a voluntary White House pact signed late last month.
quote_evidence: 'You know, fire can heat your home. It can also burn down your whole village. So that's not good. So we have to have safeguards and controls.'
'I don't think there's enough supply for it to be a bubble,' Dell said.
why_it_matters_hint: A major computer-maker's chief adds his voice for safeguards and a government role, without proposing a rule.
